text:
Anthony Cirelli missed the Lightning's games on Nov. 12 and Nov. 14 with an injury, out alongside Erik Cernak and Yanni Gourde according to several reports. He came back Tuesday against Washington and scored in a 5-2 win, his sixth goal of the season.

That's a good sign for Tampa, because Cirelli has been one of their best players at 5v5. The Lightning get 61% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and Evolving-Hockey had him in the 95th percentile among forwards for driving chances last season, though with top-1% teammates flattering his raw numbers. His scoring is fine too: 15 points in 19 games, ten in his last ten.

The odd part is that his own goals have run hot (six on 4.2 expected) while the team's have run cold around him: Tampa has scored 6.4 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. Those usually even out. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flags a signature worth watching: 20% of his setups go across the royal road, the side-to-side pass that moves a goalie, against 7% for a typical forward.
headline: Cirelli is back, and still unlucky
